claims.text: LLMs evaluated for clinical note generation demonstrated an overall sentence-level hallucination rate of 1.47%.
LLMs evaluated for clinical note generation demonstrated an overall sentence-level omission rate of 3.45%.
44% of sentences containing hallucinations in LLM-generated clinical notes were classified as major errors capable of impacting patient diagnosis or management.
Refining prompts from Experiment 3 to Experiment 8 reduced the incidence of major hallucinations by 75%.
Incorporating chain-of-thought fact atomisation prior to note generation increased major hallucinations from 4 to 25 compared to structured prompts.
Iteratively refining prompts with function calling completely eliminated major omissions, reducing them from 61 to 0 across iterations.

evidence.description: Of 12,999 sentences in 450 clinical notes, 191 sentences had hallucinations (1.47%).
Of the 49,590 sentences from consultation transcripts, 1712 sentences were omitted (3.45%).
Of 191 hallucination sentences, 84 sentences (44%) were major (could impact patient diagnosis and management if left uncorrected).
The change in the prompt from Experiments 3 to 8 reduced the incidence of major hallucinations by 75% (from 4 to 1).
Comparing Experiment 5 to Experiment 3, major hallucinations increased from 4 to 25.
From Experiments 6 to 11, major omissions decreased from 61 to 0.

methodologies.name: CREOLA Clinical Evaluation Framework and Platform
methodologies.description: A multi-component evaluation methodology combining a clinical error taxonomy, iterative prompting experiments, medical device-inspired safety risk assessment, and a clinician-in-the-loop web interface.
conditions: Clinician double-review with senior clinician consolidation

limitations.text: Automated metrics such as ROUGE, BLEU, and BERT-score fail to capture semantic nuances and clinical accuracy required for healthcare content.
Existing QA benchmarks do not assess clinical summarisation or medical document generation capabilities.
The sample size of medical transcripts used across experiments was relatively small due to annotation volume trade-offs.
Evaluation was restricted to a single model architecture (GPT-4).
The study only evaluated direct prompting strategies rather than advanced retrieval or knowledge graph methods.

future_work.text: Applying the clinical safety evaluation framework across different LLM architectures (e.g., open-source models) and advanced techniques like RAG, Chain-of-Thought, or Knowledge Graphs.
Developing automated LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation models for scalable screening, supervised by human clinicians reviewing output sub-samples.
